summary: James Burnes worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh and received an LL.D. from the University of Glasgow around 1834.

James C. Dobbins specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Yale University in 1984 and served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College (attested 2015–2019).

James C. Harle worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned degrees from Princeton University and the University of Oxford, serving as Assistant to Dean at Princeton (1947–1949) and Assistant Keeper (1960) and Keeper (1967–1987) at the Ashmolean Museum.

James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland was an Indologist who studied at East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck. He served as Registrar at Calcutta High Court (1810) and Principal and Superintendent at Hooghly Mohsin College (1839).

James Darmesteter specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying under Abel Bergaigne, Michel Bréal, and Eugène-Armand Hauvette-Besnault. He taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and was Professor at Collège de France (1885–1894).

James Drummond Anderson worked in Indology and linguistics. He served in the Indian Civil Service (1875–1900), studied at Cheltenham College, Rugby School, and Cambridge (M.A. 1909), and was appointed University Lecturer in Bengali at Cambridge in 1907.

James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1961–1964) under Sheldon Pollock. He joined the University of Iowa in 1971, where he became Professor Emeritus.
James Dwight Dana studied at Yale College (~1830–1833). He held a post at Yale University from around 1850 to 1892, where he taught Charles Rockwell Lanman.
James Fairbrother Edwards worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Handsworth Theological College (~1904–1907) and served as Principal of the United Theological College, Pune, in 1930.

James Fergusson worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal High School, became a member of the Royal Asiatic Society in 1840, and served as secretary to A. H. Layard at the Office of Works in 1868.

James Fieser is a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Berea College and Purdue University. He has held academic posts at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, and the University of Tennessee at Martin around 1992.

James Fuller Blumhardt worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Lecturer in Bengali at the University of Cambridge (1883–1888), Lecturer at University College London (~1889–1921), and worked in the British Museum's Oriental manuscripts department (~1894–1921).

James G. Mullens works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Simon Fraser, Victoria, and McMaster universities (PhD 1994), he studied under Graeme MacQueen, Yün-hua Jan, and John G. Arapura, joining the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

James Grant Liston Garthwaite worked in linguistics and Indology. After earning a B.A. at Westminster College, London, he served as a missionary and teacher with the Basel Mission (~1857–1860) and became a Fellow of the University of Madras (1884).
James Grant Stephen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1856–1861, B.A.). He later served as Lecturer in Hindustani at Cambridge from 1860 to 1863.

James Gray was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He taught at Akyab Government High School (1872), was Professor of Pāli at Basic Education High School No. 1 Dagon, and served as Professor of Pali at Rangoon University (~1884–1905).

James H. Austin is a neurologist who also worked in Buddhist studies, studying under Nanrei Sohaku Kobori and Katsujo Terayama. He held posts at Oregon Health & Science University (~1955–1963) and the University of Colorado (~1967–1992).

James Hadley worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Fairfield Academy and Yale (B.A. 1844) under Edward Elbridge Salisbury, tutoring at Middlebury (1845) before serving as an Assistant Professor at Yale from 1845 to 1872.

James Hair Maclean was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Glasgow, the University of Oxford, and the University of Jena. In 1895, he served as a missionary for the United Free Church of Scotland.

James Haughton Woods worked in Indology and philosophy. Educated at Harvard, Berlin, Oxford, and Strasbourg (Ph.D. 1897), he studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman, Paul Deussen, and Arthur Venis, and served as a professor at Harvard (1913–1934).
